mainTopic: Running a צדקה fund, binding town agreements, checking poor people, minimum gifts, and the greatness of צדקה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about running a צדקה fund as one purse with a stipulation. רב אשי then says he needs no stipulation, because donors rely on his judgment. Two butchers agreed to punish whoever worked on the other's day; רבא made the one who tore the hide pay, and רב פפא explains that such agreements need an אדם חשוב's approval when one is present. A ברייתא teaches that we do not audit גבאי צדקה, and רבי אלעזר adds that you should still tie up and count your money. רב הונא and רב יהודה argue over whether to check a poor person asking for food or for clothing, and a ברייתא sides with רב יהודה. A משנה sets the minimum gift for a traveling poor person, and רב פפא and רב סמא clarify that even one going door to door gets a small gift. The amud closes with praise of צדקה from רב אסי, רבי אלעזר and רבא, and a teaching רבא was told that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He too made one purse and stipulated about it
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier story: following the advice he heard, this sage also kept a single charity purse and made a stipulation about how it could be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...and stipulate about it.' He too made one purse and stipulated about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that began before this section. The sage followed the advice and ran his צדקה fund as one purse, with a stipulation about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collected money normally has to go to the purpose it was given for. With a stipulation made up front, one shared purse can be used wherever it is needed. This sets up רב אשי's comment in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A purse; here, a charity fund
Made a stipulation, set a condition in advance

phrases.english: and stipulate about it."
phrases.notes: These words close a quote of the advice from the earlier story: keep one purse and set a condition on it.

phrases.english: He too made one purse,
and stipulated about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיהוּ נָמֵי עֲבַד חַד כִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a story that started before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One combined צדקה purse is allowed when a stipulation was made about it.

steps.title: רב אשי needs no stipulation at all
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says he does not even need a stipulation, because donors give with the understanding that he will decide who receives the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I don't even need to stipulate, because whoever gives, gives relying on my judgment, and I give it to whomever I want.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds his own view: in his case no stipulation is needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stipulation is only needed to free the money from what the donors had in mind. When the donors themselves rely on the collector's judgment, he is already free to give as he sees fit. This depends on how much the community trusts the person running the fund.

keyTerms.meaning: Relying on my judgment or decision

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rules for using צדקה money follow what the donors had in mind when they gave.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I don't even need to make a stipulation,
because whoever comes to give
comes relying on my judgment,
and I give it to whomever I want.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲנָא – אַתְנוֹיֵי נָמֵי לָא צְרִיכְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one step further than the previous step: no stipulation is needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When donors rely on the collector's judgment, he may give the money as he sees fit without any stipulation.

steps.title: The two butchers and the torn hide
steps.stepSummary: Two butchers agreed that if either worked on the other's day, his animal's hide would be torn. One broke the deal, the other tore his hide, and רבא made the hide-tearer pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two butchers agreed that whoever worked on the other's assigned day would have his hide torn. One of them did, and his hide was torn. They came before רבא, and רבא made them pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. Two butchers made a private penalty agreement, one of them enforced it, and רבא ruled that the one who tore the hide must pay for the damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think an agreed penalty lets the other side carry it out. רבא did not let the agreement protect the one who tore the hide, so he is treated as a person who caused damage. The reason for this ruling becomes the next debate.

phrases.english: There were these two butchers
who made an agreement with each other,
that whoever works on his fellow's day,
they will tear up his hide.
One of them went
and worked on his fellow's day;
they tore up his hide.
They came before Rava,
and Rava obligated them to pay.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the side that tore the hide; they pay the butcher whose hide was ruined.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בֵּי תְרֵי טַבָּחֵי דְּעָבְדִי עִנְיָינָא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about agreements between members of a town
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא obligated the one who tore the hide to pay, even though there had been a penalty agreement.

steps.title: Townspeople are allowed to fine violators
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר בר שלמיא challenges רבא from the ברייתא that lets townspeople fine those who break their rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר בר שלמיא objected to רבא: But it was taught that townspeople may fine people for breaking their agreed rules!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר בר שלמיא challenges רבא's ruling. A ברייתא says townspeople have the power to penalize anyone who breaks their rules, so the butchers' penalty should have been valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a town may fine those who break its rules, a group of tradesmen should also be able to enforce their own agreed penalty. In that case the one who tore the hide only did what the agreement allowed, and he should not have to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a תנאי source
To fine people for breaking their set terms

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya raised an objection to Rava:
"And to fine for violating their set terms"!
phrases.notes: He is quoting the ברייתא that lists the powers the people of a town have, including fining those who break their rules.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the hide-tearer must pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives townspeople the power to fine those who break their rules, so the butchers' agreed penalty should be binding and there should be no payment.

steps.title: An important person must approve the agreement
steps.stepSummary: רבא stayed silent. רב פפא explains that he was right to say nothing, because the townspeople's power to fine only applies when there is no אדם חשוב in the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא did not answer him. רב פפא said: He was right not to answer. That rule applies only where there is no important person. Where there is an important person, they cannot make binding rules by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gave no reply, and רב פפא explains why the challenge was not a real problem. The power to fine is limited to places with no אדם חשוב, and the butchers had not made their agreement with such a person's approval.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא separates two kinds of situations. Where no recognized leader is present, the townspeople's own agreements are binding. Where an אדם חשוב is present, his approval is needed, and the butchers acted without it, so their penalty had no force and רבא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He did well, he was right
An important person, a recognized leader or scholar
It is not within their power

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's silence does not mean he had no answer. רב פפא explains that the challenge did not apply here at all.
steps.whatToRemember: Townspeople and tradesmen can make binding rules with penalties, but if an אדם חשוב is present, their rules need his approval to be valid.

phrases.english: Rava did not answer him.
Rav Pappa said:
He did well
in not answering him anything;
this applies only where
there is no important person,
but where there is an important person,
it is not in their power to make stipulations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שַׁפִּיר עֲבַד דְּלָא אַהְדַּר לֵיהּ מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The townspeople's power to fine applies everywhere, so the butchers' penalty is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: That power applies only where there is no אדם חשוב. Where one is present, their agreements need his approval, so the butchers' penalty was not binding.

steps.title: We do not audit charity collectors or Temple treasurers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that we do not demand an accounting from גבאי צדקה about charity money, or from the גזברין about הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We do not make calculations about charity with the charity collectors, nor about consecrated property with the treasurers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. Charity collectors and Temple treasurers are trusted, so we do not check their accounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling places גבאי צדקה on the same level of trust as the Temple's גזברין. No one goes back over the figures for what came in and what went out.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught, the opening of a ברייתא
Make calculations, go over the accounts

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We do not make calculations concerning charity
with the charity collectors,
nor concerning consecrated property with the treasurers.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין בִּצְדָקָה עִם גַּבָּאֵי צְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about the trustworthiness of those who handle צדקה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Charity collectors and Temple treasurers are not audited.

steps.title: A hint from the Temple repair workers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא admits there is no real proof, but brings a hint from a פסוק in מלכים: the workers repairing the Temple were not audited, because they acted faithfully.
steps.simpleTranslation: Although there is no proof for this, there is a hint, as the פסוק says: 'And they did not reckon with the men into whose hand they gave the money to pay the workers, for they acted faithfully.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא supports its rule with a פסוק. It clearly labels this as only a hint, not a full proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the days of the Temple repairs, the people who handled the money were not asked for an accounting because they were trusted. That fits the rule of not auditing trusted public officials. It is called a זכר לדבר because the פסוק describes what was done then and does not command it.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no proof for the matter
A hint or allusion for the matter

steps.whatToRemember: Trusted public officials who handle צדקה and הקדש are not audited, with a hint from the Temple repairs in מלכים ב.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: And even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint for the matter,
as it is said:
"And they did not reckon with the men

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר יִתְּנוּ אֶת הַכֶּסֶף עַל יָדָם
phrases.english: into whose hand they gave the money
to give to those doing the work,
for they acted in faithfulness."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 12:16

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule in step 6
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we do not audit גבאי צדקה or גזברין
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 12:16: those who handled the money for the Temple repairs were not audited because they acted faithfully

steps.title: Even with a trusted treasurer, tie up and count your money
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that even if a person has a fully trusted treasurer at home, he should still tie up and count his money. He learns this from the same פסוק about the Temple money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Even if a person has a trustworthy treasurer in his house, he should tie up his money and count it, as the פסוק says: 'They tied it up and counted it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds a practical lesson to the Temple story. Even though trusted people are not audited, the money should still be bundled and counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 showed that the Temple workers were not checked because they were faithful. רבי אלעזר points out that the same story begins with the money being tied up and counted before it was handed over. Trusting someone does not mean being careless with the money.

keyTerms.meaning: treasurer, the person who manages money
he should tie up (bundle the money)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a model for honest money management. You can trust someone and still keep a clear record.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לָאָדָם
phrases.english: Even though a person has
a trustworthy treasurer in his house,
he should tie up his money and count it,
as it is said: 'And they tied it up and counted it.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 12:11. This is from the same Temple story as the last step, a few verses earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לָאָדָם גִּזְבָּר נֶאֱמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק from step 7. Trusted workers were not audited, but the money was still counted first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with a trusted treasurer, a person should tie up and count his money.

steps.title: Check requests for food, not for clothing
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that גבאי צדקה check whether a person asking for food is really poor, but they do not check someone asking for clothing. He says this can be shown by a פסוק or by a סברא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: We check a person asking for food, but we do not check a person asking for clothing. You can learn this from a פסוק, or you can learn it from logic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question: when do charity collectors check that a poor person is honest? רב הונא gives his ruling and announces two possible sources, which the next steps will explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking means asking questions to make sure the person is truly needy before giving. רב הונא makes a clear difference between food and clothing. The phrase 'if you want, say' tells us that two separate reasons are coming.

keyTerms.meaning: we check / investigate (whether he is truly poor)
if you want, say (introduces one of two possible reasons)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
We check someone who asks for food,
but we do not check someone who asks for clothing.
If you want, say it comes from a verse,
and if you want, say it comes from logic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בּוֹדְקִין לִמְזוֹנוֹת, וְאֵין בּוֹדְקִין לִכְסוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in צדקה: checking the people who receive it, after the earlier steps about the people who collect it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Check someone who asks for food, but give clothing without checking.

steps.title: The logic: the person without clothes is being shamed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's סברא: a person in rags is publicly embarrassed, while a hungry person is not. So we give clothing right away, but we can take time to check someone asking for food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it from logic: this one (without clothes) is being shamed, and that one (the hungry person) is not being shamed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first support for רב הונא, the logical reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hunger is hidden, but standing in rags is a public embarrassment. Because the shame keeps going every moment we wait, we should not delay clothing him to check his story. A hungry person is not shamed in the same way, so a short check is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: a word showing something is happening right now

phrases.english: If you want, say it from logic:
this one is being shamed,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the person asking for clothing, who stands there in rags.

phrases.english: and that one is not being shamed.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the hungry person. His hunger is not on display.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא – הַאי קָא מִבַּזֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the סברא that step 9 promised.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that clothing is given without checking
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: the person without clothes suffers public shame, and the hungry person does not.

steps.title: The פסוק: check before giving bread, cover the naked right away
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's פסוק from ישעיהו: the word for 'share' your bread can be read as 'examine,' so we check first and then give. About clothing the פסוק says 'when you see' the naked, cover him, which means right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it from a פסוק: 'Is it not to share your bread with the hungry?' Read the word with a שין, meaning 'examine': check first, and then give him. And there it says: 'When you see the naked, cover him.' 'When you see' means immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second support for רב הונא, a פסוק that covers both food and clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's point is that the word is spelled with a ש, as פרש, which means 'examine,' even though it is read as פרס, 'share.' So the spelling teaches that we examine before handing out bread. For clothing, 'when you see' teaches that the moment you see him, you act, with no delay to check.

keyTerms.meaning: to share / spread out (the plain reading)
examine, look into it carefully (read with a שין)

steps.confusionAlert: The דרשה is not about a dot. רב הונא contrasts how the word is written, with a ש ('examine'), with how it is read, פרס with a ס ('share'). רב יהודה in step 14 goes by the way it is read.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, food requests are checked and clothing is given immediately, because the person in rags is shamed and because the פסוק says 'when you see.'

phrases.english: If you want, say it from a verse:
'Is it not to share your bread with the hungry?'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 58:7

phrases.english: It is written with a shin: 'examine,'
phrases.notes: Read with a shin, the word means 'look into it carefully,' not just 'share.'

phrases.english: and afterwards give him.
And there it is written:
phrases.notes: 'There' means in the same פסוק, a little further on.

phrases.english: 'When you see the naked, cover him';
'When you see': immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא – הֲלֹא פָרֹשׂ לָרָעֵב לַחְמֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second support (the פסוק) promised in step 9, after the סברא in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: Both halves of רב הונא's ruling
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 58:7: 'פרס' read as 'פרוש' (examine) for food, and 'כי תראה' (immediately) for clothing.

steps.title: רב יהודה says the opposite: check clothing, not food
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה disagrees with רב הונא. He says we check someone asking for clothing but not someone asking for food. He too has a סברא and a פסוק, which the גמרא is about to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: We check someone asking for clothing, and we do not check someone asking for food. If you want, say it from logic, and if you want, say it from a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposite opinion and announces two supports for it. This line sets up the reasons that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is a clear מחלוקת: each אמורא checks the case the other one gives right away. רב יהודה's reasons have not been given yet, so the learner should expect them in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא who disagrees with רב הונא here
we check someone asking for clothing
we do not check someone asking for food

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. רב הונא checks food, and רב יהודה checks clothing.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
We check someone who asks for clothing,
and we do not check someone who asks for food.
If you want, say it from logic,
and if you want, say it from a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: בּוֹדְקִין לִכְסוּת, וְאֵין בּוֹדְקִין לִמְזוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposite opinion to רב הונא's ruling in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Check someone asking for clothing, but give food without checking.

steps.title: רב יהודה's logic: the hungry person is the one who suffers
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's סברא: the hungry person is in pain, while the person in torn clothes is not suffering in the same way. So food is given right away, and clothing can wait for a check.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is logic: this one (the hungry person) is suffering, and that one (the person needing clothes) is not suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first support for רב יהודה: a simple piece of logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה builds his סברא the same way רב הונא did, 'this one... that one,' but his reason is suffering, not shame. For him, hunger is the real pain that can't wait. Torn clothing is not as urgent, so we have time to check first.

keyTerms.meaning: He is suffering; it causes him pain

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא's סברא in step 10 was about shame (מבזי). רב יהודה's is about suffering (מצערא). For רב יהודה, the hungry person is the one who suffers, so food can't wait.

phrases.english: If you want, say it comes from logic:
this one is suffering,
phrases.notes: For רב יהודה, 'this one' is the hungry person.

phrases.english: and that one is not suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fulfills the promise from step 12 that רב יהודה has a סברא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that food is given without checking and clothing is checked
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: hunger causes real suffering, torn clothing less so

steps.title: רב יהודה's פסוק: share bread right away, cover the naked once it is clear
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads 'פרוס' as it is pronounced, 'share,' meaning give bread at once. 'When you see the naked' means once it becomes clear to you that he is truly needy, then clothe him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say it comes from a פסוק. Here it says, 'Share your bread with the hungry' — share immediately, just as we read the word. And there it says, 'When you see the naked, cover him' — when it becomes clear to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second support for רב יהודה: the same פסוק רב הונא used, but read the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא read 'פרוס' as hinting to 'check.' רב יהודה reads it plainly, 'share,' so food is given at once. He reads 'כי תראה' not as 'the moment you see him' but as 'once the truth is seen,' meaning after checking.

keyTerms.meaning: As we read it out loud
When it becomes clear to you

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא and רב יהודה both use the very same פסוק but read it in opposite directions. Their סברות differ: shame for רב הונא, suffering for רב יהודה.

phrases.english: If you want, say it comes from a verse:
Here it is written:
'Is it not to share your bread with the hungry?'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 58:7

phrases.english: share immediately, just as we read it;
and there it is written:
'When you see the naked, cover him' —
when it becomes clear to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second support for רב יהודה, after the סברא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 58:7, read as 'share at once' for bread and 'once it is clear' for clothing

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees with רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches: if he says 'clothe me,' we check him; if he says 'feed me,' we do not check.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like רב יהודה: if he said 'Cover me,' we check up on him. If he said 'Sustain me,' we do not check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב יהודה said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds outside support from a teaching of the תנאים. It backs רב יהודה's side over רב הונא's.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him

steps.whyThisMatters: Because a ברייתא supports him, רב יהודה's view gets extra weight in the argument with רב הונא.

phrases.english: It was taught in agreement with רב יהודה:
If he said 'Cover me,' we check up on him.
If he said 'Feed me,' we do not check.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רב הונא and רב יהודה argument with a ברייתא supporting רב יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same ruling

steps.title: משנה: the minimum given to a traveling poor person
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in מסכת פאה: a poor person passing through must be given at least a loaf worth a פונדיון, priced when wheat is four סאה for a סלע. If he stays the night, he gets what he needs for sleeping.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: We don't give a poor person traveling from place to place less than a loaf worth a פונדיון, when wheat is four סאה for a סלע. If he stays overnight, we give him what he needs for lodging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about the least we may give a poor traveler.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets a minimum amount of bread, tied to a set wheat price so the amount doesn't change with the market. It adds that a poor person who sleeps over also gets sleeping needs.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
We do not give less than
What is needed for sleeping over

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in פאה 8:7.

phrases.english: We do not give less to a poor person
who is traveling from place to place
than a loaf worth a פונדיון,
when wheat sells at four סאה for a סלע.
If he sleeps over, we give him what he needs for lodging.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from checking the poor to the minimum gift for a traveling poor person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveling poor person gets at least a loaf worth a פונדיון, and lodging needs if he stays the night.

steps.title: What counts as 'lodging needs'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'פרנסת לינה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'provisions for lodging'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what one phrase in the משנה means. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה didn't spell out what 'lodging needs' includes. The גמרא wants to know exactly what must be given.

phrases.english: What is 'provisions for lodging'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״פַּרְנָסַת לִינָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a term from the משנה just quoted.

steps.title: רב פפא: a bed and a pillow
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that lodging needs means a bed and a pillow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A bed and a pillow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: 'lodging needs' means something to sleep on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The term means the basic gear for sleeping, a bed and a pillow. It does not mean money or a room.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
A bed and a pillow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא פּוּרְיָא וּבֵי סַדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרנסת לינה means a bed and a pillow

steps.title: משנה continues: food for three שבת meals
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה: if the poor traveler stays for שבת, he gets food for three meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stays over שבת, we give him food for three meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה after explaining 'lodging needs.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה adds one more level: someone staying for שבת needs the three שבת meals. So he is given enough for all of them.

phrases.english: If he stays over Shabbos, we give him
food for three meals.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁבַת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ מְזוֹן שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה after the side question about lodging.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor traveler staying for Shabbos gets food for three meals.

steps.title: ברייתא: we don't have to tend to one who goes door to door
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a poor person is going from door to door, the community does not have to tend to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if he was going around to the doors, we do not need to tend to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ברייתא that limits the משנה's rule. The next steps will explain what this limit really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said what to give a traveling poor person. The ברייתא says that a person already collecting from house to house does not need to be tended to. It is not yet clear if this means nothing at all, and the story that follows clears that up.

keyTerms.meaning: Going around from door to door
We do not have to tend to him

phrases.english: It was taught:
If he was going around to the doors,
we do not need to tend to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא אִם הָיָה מְחַזֵּיר עַל הַפְּתָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the משנה's rule for poor travelers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor person going door to door does not need to be tended to.

steps.title: Story: רב פפא does not help a door-to-door poor man
steps.stepSummary: A poor man who went door to door came to רב פפא, and רב פפא did not help him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain poor man who went around to the doors came before רב פפא, and he did not tend to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that tests the ברייתא's rule in real life. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא seems to be following the ברייתא exactly as written: no help for someone going door to door. The story is about to ask whether that is the right way to read the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not tend to him

phrases.english: A certain poor man
who was going around to the doors
came before רב פפא,
and he did not tend to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא עַנְיָא דַּהֲוָה מְחַזֵּיר עַל הַפְּתָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real case applying the ברייתא of step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא gave nothing to a door-to-door poor man.

steps.title: רב סמא: if you don't help him, should he die?
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא protests to רב פפא: if you won't help him, nobody else will either. Should he be left to die?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סמא son of רב ייבא said to רב פפא: If the master doesn't tend to him, no other person will tend to him. Should he die?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב סמא challenges רב פפא for not helping the poor man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is practical: if a leading person in charge of צדקה turns him away, others will follow, and the man could starve. Giving nothing can't be right.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: רב סמא son of רב ייבא said to רב פפא:
If the master does not tend to him,
no other person will tend to him!
Should he just die?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָר לָא מִזְדְּקִיק לֵיהּ אִינָשׁ אַחֲרִינָא לָא מִזְדְּקִיק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's action in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's refusal to give the door-to-door poor man anything
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the main צדקה authority gives nothing, no one will, and the poor man could die.

steps.title: רב פפא points to the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא defends himself: doesn't the ברייתא say we don't tend to someone going door to door?
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: if a poor person was going around to the doors, we don't tend to him!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back against רב סמא by quoting the ברייתא from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's point is that he did just what the ברייתא says. So רב סמא's complaint seems to go against a written teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't name the speaker, but this is רב פפא defending himself.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה עָנִי הַמְחַזֵּיר עַל הַפְּתָחִים –
phrases.english: If a poor person was going around to the doors,
we do not tend to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב סמא's protest with the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב סמא's demand that the poor man be helped
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא clearly says not to tend to someone going door to door.

steps.title: רב סמא: no big gift, but still a small gift
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא explains the ברייתא: we don't give a door-to-door poor person a big gift, but we do give him a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We don't tend to him with a big gift, but we do tend to him with a small gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רב סמא answers by explaining what the ברייתא really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was never saying 'give nothing.' It only means the full, large gift isn't required, since he is already collecting from many homes. A small gift is still given, so no one is left to starve.
steps.whatToRemember: A poor person going door to door still gets a small gift. The ברייתא only frees us from giving him a big one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows we never turn a poor person away with nothing, even when the law says less is needed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We do not tend to him with a big gift,
but we do tend to him with a small gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין נִזְקָקִין לוֹ לְמַתָּנָה מְרוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's ברייתא by limiting what it means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a door-to-door poor person gets nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: He gets no big gift, but he does get a small gift.

steps.title: רב אסי: give at least a third of a שקל a year
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי teaches that a person should never hold back from giving a third of a שקל a year, learned from a פסוק in נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: A person should never hold himself back from giving a third of a שקל a year, as it says: 'And we took upon ourselves מצוות, to charge ourselves a third of a שקל a year for the service of the House of our God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from רב אסי about a yearly minimum for giving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי sets a basic yearly amount that everyone should give. He learns it from the people in the time of נחמיה, who took on a yearly third of a שקל.

phrases.english: רב אסי said:
A person should never hold himself back
from giving a third of a שקל a year,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; it's part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: as it is said:
'And we took upon ourselves מצוות,
phrases.notes: נחמיה 10:33

phrases.english: to charge ourselves a third of a שקל each year
for the service of the House of our God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי לְעוֹלָם אַל יִמְנַע אָדָם עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about giving, after the section on the poor traveler.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should give at least a third of a שקל a year.

steps.title: רב אסי: צדקה equals all the מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי teaches that צדקה is equal to all the other מצוות, because the פסוק says 'מצוות' (plural) and not 'מצוה' (single).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי said: צדקה is equal to all the מצוות, as it says: 'And we took upon ourselves מצוות.' It doesn't say 'a מצוה' here, but 'מצוות.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives a second teaching from the same פסוק, about how great צדקה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about one act of giving, yet it calls it 'מצוות,' plural. רב אסי learns from this that this one act of giving is worth as much as many מצוות, meaning all of them.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי learns two things from one פסוק in נחמיה: give at least a third of a שקל a year, and צדקה is equal to all the מצוות.

phrases.english: And רב אסי said:
צדקה is equal to all the מצוות,
as it is said: 'And we took upon ourselves מצוות, etc.'
It does not say 'a מצוה' here,
but rather 'מצוות.'
phrases.notes: One act of giving is called by a plural word, so it counts like many מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב אַסִּי שְׁקוּלָה צְדָקָה כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by רב אסי from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקה is equal to all the other מצוות, learned from the plural word 'מצוות.'

steps.title: Getting others to give is greater than giving
steps.stepSummary: After a memory list of key words, רבי אלעזר teaches that someone who causes others to give צדקה is greater than the person who gives. He proves it from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory list: Greater, Temple, משה.) רבי אלעזר said: The one who gets others to do good is greater than the one who does it, as it says: 'The making of צדקה will be peace, and the work of צדקה will be quiet and safety forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short memory list for the coming teachings. Then רבי אלעזר teaches that a person who gets others to give צדקה is greater than the giver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions two things: מעשה הצדקה, which he reads as making others do צדקה, and עבודת הצדקה, which is doing the work yourself. The first is paired with 'peace,' and the second with 'quiet and safety.' רבי אלעזר reads this as showing that the one who causes others to give gets the greater reward.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory list of key words to help remember the order of the teachings
The one who gets others to act, for example a צדקה collector
The one who does the act himself
Literally 'the making of צדקה', read here as causing others to give
The work of צדקה, meaning giving it yourself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read הַמְעַשֶּׂה as 'the one who does.' It means the one who gets OTHERS to do. That is the whole point of the teaching.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basis for the great value placed on צדקה collectors and fundraisers. They get credit for everyone they move to give.

phrases.english: (Memory list: Greater, Temple, Moshe)
Rabbi Elazar said:
The one who gets others to do is greater than the one who does,
as it says: 'And the making of righteousness will be peace,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 32:17

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲבֹדַת הַצְּדָקָה הַשְׁקֵט וָבֶטַח עַד עוֹלָם״;
phrases.english: and the work of righteousness, quiet and safety forever.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: גָּדוֹל הַמְעַשֶּׂה יוֹתֵר מִן הָעוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings praising צדקה that רב אסי began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who causes others to give צדקה is greater than one who gives himself.

steps.title: Giving willingly versus giving against your will
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ישעיהו is read two ways. If a person merits, he willingly shares his bread with the hungry. If he doesn't merit, he is forced to bring wanderers into his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he merits: 'Share your bread with the hungry.' If he does not merit: 'You will bring wandering poor people into your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads two parts of one פסוק as two possible outcomes. Someone who merits gives willingly, and someone who doesn't ends up having to give anyway, against his will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both parts of the פסוק involve providing for others. The difference is whether it happens by choice or by force. The message is that the giving will happen either way, so it is better to do it willingly and get the credit.

keyTerms.meaning: He merits, meaning he is worthy
Share your bread with the hungry

phrases.english: If he merits: 'Is it not to share your bread with the hungry?'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 58:7

phrases.english: If he does not merit: 'And wandering poor people you will bring into your house.'
phrases.notes: This is the next part of the same פסוק. Here it describes having to take people in against your will.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָה – הֲלֹא פָרֹשׂ לָרָעֵב לַחְמֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching about צדקה: giving by choice versus being forced to give.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who merits gives willingly; one who doesn't is forced to provide for others anyway.

steps.title: רבא urges the people of מחוזא to give to each other
steps.stepSummary: רבא begs the people of מחוזא to be generous with one another, so that they will have peace with the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to the people of מחוזא: Please, I beg you, act with charity toward one another, so that you will have peace with the government.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא puts the previous teaching into practice. He urges his community to give to each other so they won't suffer at the hands of the government.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the idea from the last step: money that isn't given willingly may end up being taken. By being generous with each other, the people of מחוזא could avoid trouble with the authorities. The word 'peace' also echoes the פסוק in step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of מחוזא, the town where רבא lived

phrases.english: Rava said to the people of Mechoza:
Please, I beg of you,
act toward one another,
phrases.notes: He means give צדקה to each other. The word עושו echoes the 'doing' of צדקה from the earlier teaching.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלֶיהְוֵי לְכוּ שְׁלָמָא בְּמַלְכוּתָא.
phrases.english: so that you will have peace with the government.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא לִבְנֵי מָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical application of giving willingly so as not to be forced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Generosity toward one another brings peace with the government.

steps.title: צדקה replaces the שקל after the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that when the בית המקדש stood, giving the שקל brought forgiveness. Now that it is gone, giving צדקה is good, and if people don't give, the nations take their money by force.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: When the בית המקדש stood, a person gave his שקל and was forgiven. Now that there is no בית המקדש, if people give צדקה, good. If not, the nations come and take money by force.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the 'Temple' teaching from the memory list. רבי אלעזר compares the שקל of the בית המקדש times to צדקה today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שקל used to bring atonement. Today צדקה fills that role. If people won't give, the money will be taken anyway by the nations, the same 'give willingly or be forced' idea from step 28.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
When the Temple is standing,
a person gives his shekel and receives atonement;
now that the Temple is not standing,
if they give charity, good;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו – בָּאִין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְנוֹטְלִין בִּזְרוֹעַ.
phrases.english: and if not, the nations of the world come and take by force.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second teaching of רבי אלעזר, matching the 'Temple' word in the memory list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Today צדקה takes the place of the שקל; if not given willingly, money is taken by force.

steps.title: Money taken by force still counts as צדקה
steps.stepSummary: Even money taken by force is counted as צדקה, as the פסוק says, 'your oppressors, צדקה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And even so, it is counted for them as צדקה, as it says: 'And your oppressors, צדקה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching adds a comforting point: even when the money is taken by force, it is still credited as צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step sounded like a punishment. This step softens it: the פסוק links 'your oppressors' with 'צדקה,' showing that what oppressors take is still counted as צדקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Your oppressors, the ones who force you to pay

steps.whatToRemember: צדקה is precious in every form: getting others to give is greatest, giving willingly is best, and even money taken by force is still credited as צדקה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן נֶחְשָׁב לָהֶן לִצְדָקָה –
phrases.english: And even so, it is counted for them as charity,
as it says: 'And your oppressors, righteousness.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 60:17

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן נֶחְשָׁב לָהֶן לִצְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to step 30: money taken by force is still credited as צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money taken by force is still credited as צדקה.

steps.title: רבא begins telling something he was told
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to report a teaching that a little child told him. The rest continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This matter was told to me by the little child.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא is introducing a teaching he heard, and the content comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is taught yet. This line tells us who the source of the next teaching is, and the actual content comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This matter was told to me by the infant
phrases.notes: Here עולא means 'the little child,' not the sage עולא. The sentence keeps going on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מִילְּתָא אִישְׁתַּעִי לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up the next teaching in the series about צדקה.
